source: verified consumer/maker EEG stack — the real open hardware + software for a brain-signal input source.

components.name: OpenBCI Cyton Biosensing Board (8-channel)
components.what: Arduino-compatible 8-channel, 250 Hz open-hardware bioamplifier that samples EEG/EMG/ECG and streams over RFDuino radio, the reference maker-grade research EEG board.

components.name: OpenBCI Ganglion Board (4-channel)
components.what: Low-cost 4-channel open-hardware bioamplifier with onboard accelerometer and BLE, the cheapest OpenBCI entry point for EEG/EMG/ECG capture.

components.name: Muse 2 EEG headband (Interaxon)
components.what: Consumer dry-electrode 4-channel EEG headband (TP9/AF7/AF8/TP10) with BLE, the most affordable off-the-shelf brain-sensing wearable and the easiest on-ramp for a maker EEG input.
components.license: Proprietary consumer hardware (raw EEG accessible via community tooling, not officially open)

components.name: BrainFlow
components.what: Board-agnostic SDK to acquire, parse and analyze EEG/EMG/ECG from OpenBCI, Muse and 30+ other biosensors through one uniform API, installed with a single pip command.

components.name: muse-lsl (muselsl)
components.what: Python package that connects to Muse headbands over BLE and streams, visualizes and records their EEG via Lab Streaming Layer, the standard bridge from a consumer Muse into an LSL pipeline.

components.name: Lab Streaming Layer (LSL / pylsl)
components.what: Open middleware for unified, time-synchronized real-time collection of measurement time series over a network, the de-facto transport that lets EEG streams interoperate with other signals and recorders.

components.name: BrainPad (example EEG intent-classification repo)
components.what: Open example project that classifies motor-imagery EEG from an OpenBCI Cyton board with a TensorFlow/Keras deep-learning pipeline, a concrete real-world template for turning brain signal into discrete intents.
